slides.title: Who are you with other people, now that you've met yourself?

body.text: This is using both hands to get close.

items: Whoever first gets an underhook and then grabs the head, waist, or a leg wins. The same rule applies to both players.

body.text: This is catching an arm and locking hands.

items: The bottom player wins by sliding an arm under the top player's armpit after his hand touches the mat, then locking his hands.
The top player wins by standing up and pushing the bottom player's knees down to open his legs.

body.text: This is sitting on top of his belly.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps an arm under one of the bottom player's elbows.
The bottom player wins by touching both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight you both fought for the same grip. What got you close?

options.text: Gripping his wrists and elbows on purpose.

options.feedback: Grabbing anything is not the same as on purpose.

options.text: Pushing him away to make space.
options.feedback: Pushing away is the opposite of getting close.

slides.bridge: Who you are with other people shows in how you make contact.
